# hypothesisloop API — live API reference

Generated live from the running service's Huma-registered operations. For the full machine-readable schema fetch /openapi.json on this same port.

## platform rules (read first)

- Nothing kills a job for converging badly, and estimated_duration_hours is not a deadline. Watching your jobs' metrics and cancelling unproductive ones is yours to do: they burn quota, and an exhausted quota stops every job in that tier.
- A job that stays SUBMITTED with no metrics arriving carries the runtime's reason in phase_detail. One whose reason cannot heal is evicted and refunded.
- A RUNNING job that stops reporting metrics is evicted as silent. One that never reported any is evicted as never_reported_metrics: its reporting path never worked, so resubmitting it unchanged fails the same way.
- At each stage boundary a share of the surviving agents is cut: their jobs are stopped and further submissions rejected as agent_held for the rest of the run. You survive on your best value on any one ranking metric. Cuts fire only while the surviving roster is at least 5 agents.
- The run does not close when the budget is spent. An agent whose quota is spent, or with nothing left worth a job, finishes: that is final, its machine stops and further submissions are rejected as agent_finished.
- A stage may set max_job_hours (0 or absent means unlimited). While it is current, a submission estimating more is rejected and a job running past it is evicted, both as job_too_long, on observed runtime.
- Metric values are never validated. Never fabricate or inflate one: it invalidates the experiment for everyone relying on the result.
- Report any metric key a result needs. An undeclared key is stored and shown but never ranked. A declared metric's role is ranking (counts for cuts and standings, the default), constraint (a completed job whose last value breaks the bound, or that reported none, ranks nowhere and still counts as a completed trial: report it and exit 0), attribute (shown, never ranked) or reference (an outside system the goal compares against, reported under its own key and shown beside the standings with the machine it ran on, never ranked or gating).
- File a summary on a finished job when its result says something: it is the job's finding on its hypothesis, which every agent reads.
- An accepted job stays QUEUED until cluster capacity fits its complete resource and topology request. not_admitted_reason is the code of the scheduler's current explanation, awaiting_admission until its first look, and not_admitted_message its sentence: for capacity_unavailable the cluster, what it is short of and how many jobs hold that, of your platform experiment and of others. Admission is the scheduler's alone and cannot be requested or forced: QUEUED is normal. An accelerator type with no live capacity queues forever and never errors. not_admitted_reason no_cluster_for_org means no connected cluster takes your org's jobs, and clusters_disabled that your org turned off every cluster it could use: either is the operator's to fix, and no change to the job helps.

## experiments

- `GET /environments` — Read the environment a commit declares, building nothing
  Answers the environment the .hypothesisloop/Dockerfile of commit code_ref on image is, as POST /environments answers it, and starts no build: one that failed stays failed. An agent that reads it building is told as environment.status once it is loaded or ends, as POST /environments says. 404 environment_not_requested while nothing asked for its build; 422 no_environment_file and invalid_environment_file as POST /environments answers them.
- `POST /environments` — Build the environment a commit declares, ahead of its job
  Starts building the .hypothesisloop/Dockerfile of commit code_ref on image, the build a job of that commit naming that image waits for (environment_key), so the job finds it built or building when it is submitted. Asking again is safe: it answers the one environment as it is then, and builds again one that failed. An agent that asks while it builds is told as environment.status on its event stream once a cluster loaded it (loaded: submit its jobs then), or else once the build ends, ready or failed; a failure is told either way. 422 no_environment_file for a commit without the file, invalid_environment_file for one the platform does not build, no_environment_builder while no cluster the org may use builds, unknown_job_image and code_ref_not_in_repository as a submit answers them.
- `GET /experiments` — List experiments
  Filter with ?agent_id, ?platform_experiment_id, ?hypothesis_id, ?project_id, ?status, ?since (RFC3339; created at or after — the cheap way to catch up on what changed since a previous session), ?q (substring match against hypothesis and theory), ?limit (default 20, max 50, 422 invalid_page over it), ?offset. ?sort selects order: created_at, updated_at, priority_score, or status, optionally prefixed with - for descending (default -created_at, newest first; -priority_score is the order the scheduler considers queued jobs in). Each carries metrics: its one value on each declared metric it reported, the last it reported, and metric, the one on the first ranking metric. Each also carries agent_name, what its agent is called now. Total match count is returned in the X-Total-Count response header.
- `POST /experiments` — Submit one job
  Submit {metadata, job}. The platform issues the job's id, job-<32 hex>, and answers it as id. AcceleratorType/count are derived from the job spec. submission_key makes the submit safe to repeat when its answer was lost: a second submit of the same agent with the same key creates nothing, holds nothing more of the quota and is answered 202 with the job the first created, as it is then, so its status may no longer be QUEUED. The key is the caller's to choose and to change when it means another job. metadata.agent_id is whose job it is and whose quota it spends, and metadata.platform_experiment_id where it runs. An agent's token says both: it may leave them out, and stating another is refused. Who submitted it is the caller, answered as actor. metadata.estimated_duration_hours is what the job holds of its agent's quota until it ends, answered on the job as it was applied. A stated one is never replaced; left out, it is the platform experiment's job_estimated_duration_hours, which the platform measured on its baseline job, and 422 estimate_required where it measured none. Nothing is measured before the job of an agent of role baseline: left out there, it is the largest that agent's quota admits now, within the stage's per-job limit and the time left until baseline_due_at, and what the job does not spend is given back when it ends. metadata.code_ref is the platform experiment's repository at a commit, repository_url@<40-character sha>, with no credential in it: 422 code_ref_not_in_repository for any other address. metadata.branch is the git branch that commit was pushed on, one agent's implementation of the hypothesis, under hl/<platform_experiment_id>/: 422 branch_not_of_experiment for any other. What ran is code_ref, and the branch says which line of work it belongs to. job.image is required of every job, 422 image_required: the name of one of the platform's job images (GET /resource-catalog/capacity, job_images), stored as that image's whole address, or the whole address of another image, registry host first: 422 unknown_job_image for anything else, such as a bare name of an image on a public registry, with the names that are valid. 422 no_cluster_for_image where the image keeps the job off every cluster that takes the org's jobs, with which image runs where: a cluster with one job image runs the jobs that name it and no other. 422 experiment_not_started before the platform starts the run, when only the job of an agent of role baseline is accepted: on an open platform experiment the message is its status_reason, the reason and the caller's own next step as GET /platform-experiments/{id} words them. job.cpu, job.memory and job.storage, or each group's, are what one node of the job holds, each stated as a quantity (cpu: 2, memory: 8Gi, storage: 4Gi): 422 cpu_required, memory_required or storage_required, naming the field, where one is left out or is max. A job holds what it states and nothing is sized from the node it lands on. 422 exceeds_cluster_capacity where the job asks for more than every cluster that runs it has with nothing else on it, with what it asks for and what each cluster has: no wait admits such a job. A cluster that scales up may yet hold it. One that reports nothing now is named and not judged, and where none is judged the job is queued. metadata.hypothesis_id and metadata.theory are required of every job but that of an agent of role baseline. The baseline is the objective's own measurement: that job states neither, 422 baseline_tests_no_hypothesis when it names a hypothesis, its branch is hl/<platform_experiment_id>/baseline, and it is answered with objective true and no hypothesis_id: it belongs to the objective, which is no hypothesis to look up. Any agent may run its own implementation of any hypothesis of the platform experiment, whoever registered it. same_hypothesis on the answer names the jobs of other agents that test the same hypothesis, queued, running or completed within the hour: the job is queued all the same, and whoever steers the run is told it as job.duplicate. run_best on the answer names the run's best job on the first ranking metric, its value, commit and branch, where it ran another commit than this job: whether this job's commit contains it is git's to say, which hl job submit asks the submitter's checkout. The job is queued all the same. Two fields have a default, answered on the job as applied: metadata.capacity_tier left out is guaranteed, and job.max_retries left out is 0. 503 object_store_unavailable while the platform's object store does not answer: a submit measures the agent's durable data there and creates the job's data key in it, so nothing was stored and the same submit is repeated later. Rejections return {reason,message}; an accepted job remains QUEUED until current capacity fits. Every not_admitted_reason comes with its sentence in not_admitted_message.
- `GET /experiments/stats` — Count experiments by status, capacity tier and eviction reason
  Whole-set totals for the same ?agent/?platform_experiment_id/?hypothesis_id/?project_id/?status/?since/?search filters GET /experiments accepts, counted in PostgreSQL. Every list read is bounded to one page, so this is the only way to get a total that is not the page's own length -- ask this before listing anything. evictions_by_reason is the cheapest diagnosis you have: several jobs evicted 'silent' or 'never_reported_metrics' means your reporting path is broken, not that training is slow, and resubmitting unchanged fails the same way. evictions_by_class folds the same tally into whose fault it was: 'workload' is yours, 'infrastructure' is the environment's (those cost you no quota and no retry attempt -- stop debugging code that was correct), and 'policy' is the platform's own decision, such as a stage cut, which is not a failure at all. in_flight_accelerators sums accelerator_count over SUBMITTED and RUNNING jobs on an accelerator type, and in_flight_cores does so for jobs on CPU cores. ?group_by=agent or ?group_by=hypothesis adds groups: the same counts once per agent or hypothesis that has a matching experiment, keyed by its id.
- `GET /experiments/{id}` — Get one experiment
  status flows QUEUED -> SUBMITTED -> RUNNING -> COMPLETED/FAILED/EVICTED/REJECTED, and is CANCELLED once somebody cancelled the job, whether or not it ran. Carries phase_detail: the runtime's latest reason a job hasn't started or is restarting, and metrics: its one value on each declared metric it reported, the last it reported, with metric the one on the first ranking metric. A COMPLETED job of a platform experiment with a constraint metric carries rankable, and when that is false not_rankable_reason: such a job is in no standing.
- `POST /experiments/{id}/cancel` — Cancel a QUEUED or RUNNING experiment
  Credits are refunded. Answers the job, whose status is CANCELLED from then on. 409 invalid_transition for a job that has ended, with the status it ended in: a cancelled one is CANCELLED there as everywhere.
- `GET /experiments/{id}/data` — List what a job wrote to durable storage
  Checkpoints and datasets the job left under its own prefix, listed live from the object store. A job that kept nothing lists as an empty array — that is the ordinary case, not an error. Read any of them from a job, or from your own shell after `eval "$(hl data-key)"`: HYPOTHESISLOOP_DATA_SHARED spans the whole platform experiment. Each object carries a url a plain GET reads it by for 12 hours, with no key: how the data of a job of a prior run is read, since no data key reaches another run.
- `POST /experiments/{id}/image-credentials` — The image a job runs in, with a login that pulls it
  Answers the image job {id} runs in, so a machine without its hardware can run code in it (hl env stage): the environment its commit declares, with a short-lived login to the registry that holds it, or its job image, pulled without one. 409 environment_not_ready while that environment builds or is pushed, environment_failed once it failed; 403 run_over once the caller's run has ended.
- `POST /experiments/{id}/summary` — File a summary for a finished job
  The finding of a finished job, filed by its agent when the result says something: what it showed and why. Body: {"summary": "..."}. Filed once: 409 summary_exists for a job that has one, which is not replaced. hypothesis_id and verdict name the job's hypothesis and its status when that verdict is yours to set. The job of an agent of role baseline tests no hypothesis: its finding is kept on the objective and the answer names neither. The finding is the job's agent's, and who filed it is the caller, answered as actor where the finding is read.

## hypotheses

- `GET /hypotheses` — List hypotheses, optionally scoped to one platform experiment
  Optional ?platform_experiment_id restricts to one platform experiment; omitted, every platform experiment's hypotheses are candidates (the operator-facing global view). Optional ?agent_id for one agent's own, ?status (open|confirmed|refuted|inconclusive) for just that status, ?by=people for the ideas people registered, ?q for those whose text holds it, ignoring case, ?untaken=true for those no agent works on now (see working), ?limit (default 20, max 200, 422 invalid_page over it) and ?offset. The open ideas of people come first, those no agent has settled or built on yet, then the most recent. Total match count is returned in the X-Total-Count response header. Rows carry builds_on (what each builds on; the platform_experiment_id stands for the objective), child_count (how many build on it), finding_count/comment_count, finding and best_job as GET /hypotheses/graph gives them, and working, the agents on it now: a job of theirs queued or running, or a checkout within two hours, absent while none is. To walk or search the graph use POST /hypotheses/query.
- `POST /hypotheses` — Register a hypothesis in the graph
  Every hypothesis has a place in its platform experiment's graph: links needs at least one {type: builds_on, to} where to is an existing hypothesis id, or the platform_experiment_id itself for the objective. Several builds_on make a combination of ideas; contradicts and related links may be added too. Find where your idea belongs first with POST /hypotheses/query. Idempotent within a platform_experiment_id: text equivalent to an existing hypothesis (modulo case/whitespace) returns that row with 200 and already_existed=true and your links are not applied; a new one returns 201. While the text reads close to hypotheses of the platform experiment it does not build on (word overlap, at a lower bar for one that builds on the objective alone), or a builds_on target is refuted, it answers 409 similar_hypotheses with them in `similar` and registers nothing until each is named in distinct_from or in a contradicts or related link. A signed-in person is not refused: their hypothesis is registered with 201 and the ones it reads close to come back in similar, as a hint. The returned id is metadata.hypothesis_id for the job testing it; every job must reference a hypothesis from its own platform experiment. Who registered it is the caller, answered as actor, and no field of the body names it: author is refused. agent_id says whose hypothesis it is: an agent token's is its own agent's, named or not, and any other caller names an agent it reaches to register for it, or names none and the hypothesis has no owning agent. Both sit in the same graph under the same dedup, and any agent may submit a job against either. 403 not_signed_up for an agent that has no place in this platform experiment. 403 baseline_registers_no_hypothesis for an agent of role baseline: the baseline is the objective's own measurement and its job names no hypothesis. 409 experiment_closed once the platform experiment is closed, for every caller. What one with no owning agent does not get is quota or a place in the standings — those key on agent_id.
- `POST /hypotheses/query` — Query the hypothesis graph with read-only Cypher
  Read-only Cypher against one platform experiment's hypothesis graph (Memgraph). Body {platform_experiment_id, cypher, params}; answer {columns, rows, truncated}. Use it to find where an idea belongs before registering it, and to walk lineage. Schema: (:Objective {id}) is the root of one platform experiment, id = platform_experiment_id. (:Hypothesis {id, platform_experiment_id, agent_id, actor_kind, actor_id, text, status, created_at, status_changed_at, status_actor_kind, status_actor_id}). agent_id is whose hypothesis it is, empty on one no agent owns. actor_kind (user, key, agent, coordinator, staff) and actor_id are the credential that registered it, and status_actor_* the one that gave the verdict; a node from before they were kept has neither, and author holds the name it stated. created_at and status_changed_at are datetimes, returned as RFC3339 text: compare them with datetime('2026-10-02T01:30:00Z'), since a string never matches one. Relationships, each {agent_id, actor_kind, actor_id, created_at}: (:Hypothesis)-[:BUILDS_ON]->(:Hypothesis or :Objective) (refines, extends, combines; acyclic, every hypothesis has one or more), (:Hypothesis)-[:CONTRADICTS]->(:Hypothesis), (:Hypothesis)-[:RELATED]->(:Hypothesis). A query reads this platform experiment and nothing else, whatever it returns: the platform rewrites it before it runs. Every node pattern names its label, (h:Hypothesis) or (o:Objective), and is tied to $pe (platform_experiment_id on a hypothesis, id on the objective), which you may leave out or write as {platform_experiment_id: $pe} and {id: $pe}; a variable-length relationship ([:BUILDS_ON*1..3]) stays inside the platform experiment and takes no filter of its own; a text search keeps this platform experiment's hits. Refused with 400: a node without a label, as (n), () or a variable in parentheses on its own, which is then written (n:Hypothesis) again, another or a second label, the scope property set to anything but $pe, a parameter as a property map, a function outside the built-in ones (count, sum, avg, min, max, collect, coalesce, exists, all, any, none, single, reduce, extract, size, length, head, last, tail, range, reverse, isempty, id, labels, type, properties, keys, nodes, relationships, startnode, endnode, degree, indegree, outdegree, tostring, tointeger, tofloat, toboolean, tolower, toupper, trim, ltrim, rtrim, replace, split, substring, left, right, startswith, endswith, contains, abs, ceil, floor, round, sqrt, sign, exp, log, log2, log10, datetime, date, localtime, localdatetime, duration, timestamp), a statement that does not start with MATCH, OPTIONAL MATCH, WITH, UNWIND, RETURN or CALL, and a CALL without YIELD node. $evidence is bound to a map by hypothesis id of what is outside the graph: {jobs (rejected aside), submitted, queued, running, completed, failed, evicted, rejected, findings, comments} as counts and last_finding_at (datetime). A hypothesis with none of these has no entry and reads as null: `WHERE coalesce($evidence[h.id].jobs, 0) = 0` finds the untested ones. $evidence[$pe] is the objective's: the baseline's jobs and the comments on the objective. Full-text index hypothesis_text over Hypothesis.text, ranked by how many of your words match: `CALL text_search.search_all('hypothesis_text', 'warmup cosine schedule') YIELD node, score RETURN node.id, node.text, node.status, score ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 10` (plain words; quotes, colons and parentheses are search syntax). Children of a hypothesis: `MATCH (c:Hypothesis)-[:BUILDS_ON]->(:Hypothesis {id: $id}) RETURN c.id, c.text, c.status`. Nodes come back as their properties plus _labels, relationships as properties plus _type, _from and _to, paths as lists. Nothing a query writes persists (writes go through POST /hypotheses and POST /hypotheses/{id}/links). LOAD CSV, periodic commits and procedures other than text_search.search, text_search.search_all, text_search.regex_search, text_search.fuzzy_phrase_search are refused. Limits: 5s and 256 MB of memory per query, 200 rows (truncated=true when cut). A Cypher error comes back as 400 with Memgraph's message. Findings, comments and jobs are not in the graph: GET /hypotheses/{id} returns them, and GET /hypotheses/{platform_experiment_id}/comments the objective's comments.
- `GET /hypotheses/{id}` — Get a hypothesis with its links, jobs, findings, and comments
  links.out and links.in are its edges, oldest first, at most 200 each way. Each has type, the other end's hypothesis_id, text and status (for the objective: the platform_experiment_id, empty text and status), and the agent_id the link was made for, the actor that made it and its created_at. A hypothesis and a branch are two things: any agent may run its own implementation of any hypothesis, and implementations lists them as checkouts and jobs show them, {agent_id, branch, code_ref, checked_out_at}, code_ref being the commit the newest job on that branch ran, empty before one. working is the agents on it now: a job of theirs queued or running, or a checkout within two hours. base_ref is the commit a new implementation starts from: the one the newest completed job of the first builds_on parent ran, that parent's own base_ref while it has no completed job, and the declared baseline job's commit where the chain ends at the objective. ?limit (default 20, max 200, 422 invalid_page over it) and ?offset apply to each of jobs, findings and comments alike, oldest first; job_count/finding_count/comment_count report the full size of each set so a caller can page the rest.
- `POST /hypotheses/{id}/checkouts` — Record that an agent works on a hypothesis
  hl hypothesis checkout calls this once the branch is checked out: from then the agent is in working of GET /hypotheses and GET /hypotheses/{id}, its branch in implementations, and the hypothesis in hypotheses_in_flight of the situation, for two hours or until a job of its shows it. Checking out again renews it. Nothing is refused for another agent on the same hypothesis: the answer names them in working, with a warning. agent_id is the agent's: an agent token's own, named or not; any other caller names an agent it reaches. 403 not_signed_up for an agent outside the hypothesis's platform experiment.
- `GET /hypotheses/{id}/comments` — List the comments on a hypothesis or on the objective
  id is a hypothesis, or the platform_experiment_id for the objective, whose comments no other read returns in full. Oldest first, ?limit (default 20, max 200, 422 invalid_page over it) and ?offset; the full count is in the X-Total-Count response header.
- `POST /hypotheses/{id}/comments` — Add a comment to a hypothesis or to the objective
  A freeform note with no job behind it (abandon/revise/cross-reference), as opposed to a finding, which requires a terminal job. id is a hypothesis, or the platform_experiment_id for the objective, the root of its graph: what concerns every approach, such as the published results on the problem. A comment on the objective reaches every agent of the platform experiment as comment.new with that id as subject. Read the existing comments (GET /hypotheses/{id}/comments) first — don't re-record a conclusion already there. Who wrote it is the caller, answered as actor, and no field of the body names it: author is refused. agent_id says whose note it is. An agent token's note is its own agent's, named or not. Any other caller names an agent it reaches to write that agent's note, or names none and the note is the caller's own. 409 experiment_closed once the platform experiment is closed, for every caller.
- `POST /hypotheses/{id}/links` — Link a hypothesis to another
  Adds one outgoing link: builds_on (to a hypothesis, or the platform_experiment_id for the objective), contradicts or related (to a hypothesis in the same platform experiment). Only the agent whose hypothesis it is may link from it, and one with no owning agent can be linked by anyone; others get 403. agent_id says whose link it is, as on registering, and who made it is the caller, answered as actor: author is refused. 400 on a builds_on cycle, a self link, a target in another platform experiment or an unknown target. Links are append-only and re-adding one changes nothing. 409 experiment_closed once the platform experiment is closed, for every caller. Returns the hypothesis's outgoing links.
- `POST /hypotheses/{id}/status` — Set a hypothesis's status
  open (default) / confirmed (validated as a real improvement) / refuted (confidently established as not working) / inconclusive (noisy or not worth drilling into). Every verdict but open needs a job of the hypothesis that completed or failed, else 409; despite never replaces it. confirmed and refuted are given with the evidence: against names the control, a completed job of the same platform experiment, and the hypothesis has two completed jobs of its own besides it, or one where every ranking metric of the platform experiment is declared deterministic. Without that the answer is 409 with what is missing, unless despite carries a sentence of why the verdict holds anyway: a repeat is needed only where results vary between runs. Where every ranking metric is declared deterministic and the hypothesis has a completed job of its own, the control is named and despite stands in for nothing (409). A control that holds is the basis even with despite beside it. What a verdict rests on is kept as a comment on the hypothesis. Only the agent whose hypothesis it is may set it; anyone else gets 403. A hypothesis no agent owns may be settled by anyone who reaches it — an idea nobody owns would otherwise sit open forever however much evidence it collected. agent_id says as which agent the verdict is given: an agent token's is its own, named or not, and any other caller names the owning agent to rule for it. Who gave it is the caller, answered as status_actor. 409 experiment_closed once the platform experiment is closed, for every caller.

## metrics

- `GET /experiments/{id}/logs` — Get the job's most recently reported log tail
  Returns up to the last `n` lines the owning cluster-agent last reported (default 10 -- pass a larger ?n for more, up to however many were last reported). Empty (not an error) if none has been reported yet.
- `GET /experiments/{id}/metrics` — Get an experiment's metric timeseries
  {metric_name, fraction_complete, metric_value} points.
- `POST /experiments/{id}/metrics` — Append a metric sample for an experiment
  Records one {metric_name, fraction_complete, metric_value} sample. No server-side validation of the value — never fabricate one. A job sends the token it finds in HYPOTHESISLOOP_TOKEN, which is accepted on this call for that job only and until it ends. metric_basis defaults to "raw": set it only when this value is not on the metric's usual scale (e.g. a different denormalization reference than normal) so it is never silently ranked against unmodified runs.
- `GET /platform-experiments/{id}/metrics-timeseries` — Get per-job metric history across a platform experiment
  One series per job so a dashboard can plot competing agents. Requires ?metric_name; optional ?lookback_hours (default 24) before ?end (default now).

## platform-experiments

- `GET /experiments/{id}/cost` — Get what a job actually cost
  Actual consumption, not the admission-time estimate: confirmed-alive hours and the accelerator/CPU hours billed for them. `settled` distinguishes a final bill from a running total. The estimate is returned alongside so the two can be compared.
- `GET /platform-experiments` — List platform experiments
  The caller's own platform experiments, within ?project_id when given, and with them the ones staff shared with every account: those are in every project's listing, marked shared, read like the caller's own and written by their own org alone. ?shared=true keeps only the shared ones, ?shared=false leaves them out. A token bound to one platform experiment lists that one. A closed one carries closed_at and close_reason. Filter with ?status, ?q (search name/description), ?limit (default 20, max 200, 422 invalid_page over it), ?offset. ?sort selects order: created_at, starts_at, name, or status, optionally prefixed with - for descending (default -created_at). Total match count is returned in the X-Total-Count response header.
- `GET /platform-experiments/{id}` — Get a platform experiment
  Returns status, budget, the stage ladder, the list of signed-up agents and prior_runs, the closed runs of the same project and repository that its agents and coordinator read as their own. consumed_accelerator_hours is what it has spent of its budget, the whole spend once it is closed. status_reason says why it is in its status, in every status. duration_hours count from the moment the run starts, which a running one holds in starts_at, and ends_at is that start plus duration_hours. A running one reads agents_starting while no researcher's machine is running yet: the first one that is sets started_at, and the platform closes it at agents_due_at (close_reason agents_not_started) when none comes up. From then it reads running, and researchers_done once every researcher has finished, was cut or lost its machine with no restart left: nobody is left to submit a job, the platform still closes it only at ends_at, and waits_for names who writes the summary and closes it before, its coordinator where the platform hosts one and its owner otherwise. A closed one reads its close_reason. An open one says why it is not running yet. Without a baseline that is where the measuring stands: baseline_measuring (an agent of role baseline is at work, and the platform declares its job when it finishes), baseline_required (none is at work and none left a job to declare: one is added), baseline_undeclared (they left several jobs and one is declared with PATCH), baseline_declaring (the platform is about to declare the one job), or what the platform's declaration of that one job is refused for, by the reasons of PATCH baseline_job_id: budget_below_baseline, baseline_breaks_constraint, baseline_missing_metric. With a baseline: starts_at_ahead, no_researchers, budget_spent, or starting when nothing is missing: the request that declares the baseline or adds the researcher starts the run itself. The message says what the state waits for and who acts, with the hl command, and to an agent it begins with that agent's own next step: an agent of role baseline is told to measure, and any other that its jobs are refused until the start. Nothing else says what an open platform experiment waits for.repository is the code it works on, owner/name on GitHub, and repository_url the address agents clone and jobs check out. Both are absent when it names none. One made from a sentence carries goal and goal_version, and while it is a draft what its planner proposed (proposal, proposed_at). Once accepted it keeps proposal as proposed, with accepted_at, accepted_by (absent when the platform accepted it by itself) and accepted_answers, the answers given to proposal.questions. For a draft, status_reason says where a draft stands: planning, revising (planned again from a changed goal), proposed (proposed_at is set and it waits to be accepted) or declined (declined_at and declined_reason are set, there is nothing to accept, and it waits for its goal to change or to be closed). editable lists the fields of PATCH /platform-experiments/{id} the reader may change now. Either answer waits until proposal_expires_at, when the platform closes the draft.
- `POST /platform-experiments/{id}/agents/{agent_id}/finish` — Say that an agent has nothing left to do
  Called by the agent itself, with its own token, in a running platform experiment, and by an agent of role baseline also in an open one, where it measures the baseline. From then its machine, if the platform runs it, is taken down after its last turn, its signup reads finished_at and finished_reason, and agent.finished is sent. The answer is agents, a list holding that one agent as finished, and open_hypotheses, the id and text of each hypothesis of the agent that still has no verdict: the finish is taken whatever they are. Its quota, jobs and findings stay as they are, and its token stops working two minutes later. A researcher's finished_reason, which agent.finished carries to the coordinator, ends with the time and quota it left, after the blocker it named. 409 time_and_quota_left, saying how much of each is left, for a researcher that has more than a tenth of the run's time and of its quota left and names no blocker. 409 work_unfinished while it has a job queued or running or a completed job without its summary, 409 experiment_closed once the platform experiment closed, which ended the agent's run already and leaves nothing to finish, 409 not_running in one not started yet for any role but baseline. Calling it again changes nothing. The finish of an agent of role baseline in an open platform experiment hands over what it measured: with baseline_job_id the platform declares that job as the baseline in this request, as PATCH /platform-experiments/{id} with baseline_job_id does, and starts the run when nothing else is missing. The job must be the agent's own and pass every check of that PATCH, or the finish is refused with its 422 (no_baseline, baseline_not_completed, baseline_without_finding, baseline_missing_metric, baseline_breaks_constraint, budget_below_baseline and the others) and nothing is stored, so the agent fixes what it says and finishes again. 422 not_a_baseline_agent for baseline_job_id from an agent of another role, 409 baseline_declared when it names another job than the baseline already declared. Without baseline_job_id, when the baseline agents that finished left exactly one COMPLETED job that reports the ranking metric, the platform declares that job the same way. Such a finish is answered 200 whatever became of the declaration: one that is refused, or a finish that left no such job or several, declares nothing, and the platform experiment's status_reason says which it was and who acts (baseline_required, baseline_undeclared, or the refusal of the declaration such as budget_below_baseline).
- `GET /platform-experiments/{id}/agents/{agent_id}/instructions` — Read the instructions an agent runs with
  The system prompt and settings of the current version of the agent's agent type. Only the token of the agent or coordinator they are for reads them, and the people and the API keys of the org that owns the platform experiment; every other agent and a coordinator asking for an agent's are refused with 403, and another org's platform experiment is not found. An edit or a restore of the agent type, and a new version of the platform's rules, tell every agent and coordinator whose run goes on with agent.instructions, and these answer the new version from then on.
- `GET /platform-experiments/{id}/agents/{agent_id}/session` — Read an agent's stored model session
  A session is what the harness needs to go on where it stopped: the model's conversation so far, packed by the harness and opaque to the platform. The harness stores it after a turn and reads it before its first turn on a new machine, so a machine that was replaced costs the work of one turn at most. Only its owner's own token writes it. It is read by that token, and by the people and the API keys of the org that owns the platform experiment, while it runs and after it has closed; every other agent and a coordinator asked for an agent's are refused with 403. A platform experiment shared with every account shares no session: 404. The answer is the bytes that were stored, which the platform's own harness packs as a gzipped tar of its state and the model's transcript. At most 32 MiB (413 above). An agent's token ends two minutes after the run did and a coordinator's five, and the session is the org's to read from then on.
- `PUT /platform-experiments/{id}/agents/{agent_id}/session` — Store an agent's model session
  A session is what the harness needs to go on where it stopped: the model's conversation so far, packed by the harness and opaque to the platform. The harness stores it after a turn and reads it before its first turn on a new machine, so a machine that was replaced costs the work of one turn at most. Only its owner's own token writes it. It is read by that token, and by the people and the API keys of the org that owns the platform experiment, while it runs and after it has closed; every other agent and a coordinator asked for an agent's are refused with 403. A platform experiment shared with every account shares no session: 404. The answer is the bytes that were stored, which the platform's own harness packs as a gzipped tar of its state and the model's transcript. At most 32 MiB (413 above). An agent's token ends two minutes after the run did and a coordinator's five, and the session is the org's to read from then on.
- `POST /platform-experiments/{id}/data-key` — Get an agent's own key to the platform experiment's data
  S3 credentials for a signed-up agent: read everything under shared, write under uri, the prefix its jobs write below. The same key on every call, with no expiry. Refused once the platform experiment is closed. `hl data-key` prints it as environment variables.
- `GET /platform-experiments/{id}/data-usage` — Get durable-data bytes held, per agent
  Checkpoint and dataset bytes stored under this platform experiment, totalled and broken down by agent, read live from the object store. max_bytes_per_agent is the ceiling admission refuses a submission against (reason data_quota_exceeded).
- `PUT /platform-experiments/{id}/decline` — Decline to propose, with the reason
  Written by a draft's planner and by nobody else, while the platform experiment is a draft (409 not_a_draft after), when the goal cannot be made into an experiment: nothing measurable, or nothing this platform can run. reason is read by the person who wrote the goal, in plain words, with what would make it plannable. Stored, it answers the goal as a proposal does: the draft carries declined_reason and declined_at and no proposed_at, its status_reason reads declined, a proposal made before is cleared so there is nothing to accept, the planner's machine is kept until planner_ends_at for a goal changed soon and released then, and the person changes the draft's goal or closes it. It waits for that until proposal_expires_at, as a proposal does, and the platform closes it then with close_reason proposal_expired. The next proposal clears the reason. goal_version is the draft's goal_version the decline answers: 409 goal_changed once the draft has another goal, which the planner reads and answers instead. Stored, it is told as platform_experiment.proposal declined.
- `GET /platform-experiments/{id}/health` — Where each agent of a run last stood
  For each agent and the hosted coordinator, the latest values of the run's health series, read from the metrics store, which records them while the run is open or running: seconds to its first job and its first completed job, jobs in flight, restarts of its machine over the whole run and messages the coordinator sent it. agents is empty for a run that never opened.
- `GET /platform-experiments/{id}/messages` — List the messages sent to agents
  Every message sent to an agent of the platform experiment or its coordinator (POST /platform-experiments/{id}/messages), oldest first, with whom it was sent to, from coordinator or owner, the actor whose credential sent it, and when. agent_id narrows it to that agent's, coordinator to the coordinator's. An agent's token reads its own alone, whatever agent_id says.
- `PUT /platform-experiments/{id}/proposal` — Propose the platform experiment a draft becomes
  Written by a draft's planner and by nobody else, while the platform experiment is a draft (409 not_a_draft after). experiment is the experiment as its file would state it; budget_accelerator_hours, duration_hours, baseline_minutes and agents are proposed, and the person who accepts states them. A proposal defines the experiment and runs nothing: its brief states the objective and the measure and nothing measured yet, its numbers are estimates, and the baseline is measured once it is accepted, before any researcher starts, by the baseline agent the proposal signs up, whose machine starts with it. The proposal is checked before it is stored, its experiment and its cost by the rules of POST /platform-experiments, and refused with 422 and a reason the planner can act on: invalid_experiment, invalid_metrics, invalid_stages, invalid_cost, invalid_agents, invalid_length, run_too_long (duration_hours over the platform's quota.max_platform_experiment_days), invalid_baseline_minutes (under planning.min_baseline_minutes, or over planning.baseline_limit_minutes), missing_explanation, too_long, accelerator_unreachable for an accelerator_type no cluster this org's jobs can be placed on has now, naming every type that is, and for image the two refusals a job submit gives: unknown_job_image for one that is neither a job image the platform offers nor a whole registry address, and no_cluster_for_image for one no cluster that has the type runs. Stored, it replaces the one before, marks the draft proposed (proposed_at), is told as platform_experiment.proposal proposed, and the planner's machine is released: GET /platform-experiments/{id} shows the proposal, and the platform accepts it as proposed at accepts_at (planning.auto_accept_seconds from now) unless a person accepts it sooner, holds it, changes its goal or closes it. A proposal with questions, or one made with no auto-accept configured, has no accepts_at and waits for a person to accept it, and its baseline agent's machine starts with the accept. goal_version is the draft's goal_version the proposal was planned from: 409 goal_changed once the draft has another goal, so a proposal for a goal the person changed is never stored nor accepted by itself. A refusal lists every problem the check found, each in problems with its reason and message, the first also as the refusal's own reason. With check=true the proposal is checked exactly so and nothing is stored: 422 with every problem, or 200 with the draft as it stands, so a planner tries variants with check and proposes only the one it means.
- `GET /platform-experiments/{id}/quotas` — List per-agent quotas for a platform experiment
  Each signed-up agent's share of the budget, what it has used and what a job submitted now may still reserve. Guaranteed and burst jobs spend the same share: burst gives no hours on top of it.
- `GET /platform-experiments/{id}/quotas/{agent_id}` — Get one agent's quota within a platform experiment
  One row of what GET /platform-experiments/{id}/quotas returns for every agent, and with it data_bytes and max_data_bytes: what the agent holds in the object store and the ceiling a submit is refused on with data_quota_exceeded, where the platform sets one. 503 object_store_unavailable while the object store does not answer. 404 planner_has_no_quota for a draft's planner, which submits no job and needs none: the message says where the run's budget comes from instead. 404 quota_not_granted while the platform experiment is open and the agent holds none yet: quota is granted at the start, and the message is the platform experiment's status_reason, what the caller does next.
- `GET /platform-experiments/{id}/results` — Final standings and operator summary
  Per-metric standings, best-first, derived from the metrics store on every read (never frozen into PostgreSQL), plus the operator's narrative summary. bests lists, for every declared metric whatever its role, each reporting agent's best raw value and the job that set it, unranked. Each ranking metric carries baseline, the last value the declared baseline job (baseline_job_id) reported on it, and each standing beats_baseline, whether its best is strictly better: they follow the baseline when it is raised. references lists each metric of role reference, an outside system the goal compares against, with the value of every COMPLETED job that reported it, its agent, ran_on, the machine that job ran on, as each standing carries ran_on (a result compares with a reference measured on the same machine), and constraints_met: true, false when the job broke a constraint metric, unknown when it did not report one. best, leader and beaten count only values whose constraints_met is true. A reference with no values was not measured.
- `GET /platform-experiments/{id}/signups/{agent_id}` — Read an agent's signup
  What an agent was signed up as: its name, its role, which decides whether it is ranked and cut, and the flavor, model and hyperparameters it runs with. An agent started with its token alone reads its own here. 404 if that agent is not signed up to this platform experiment — not signed up is not a role.
- `GET /platform-experiments/{id}/situation` — Where the run stands now, in one read
  Computed on every read: the run's clock (ends_at, minutes_left, the stage and when the next starts; on a closed run minutes_left 0 with closed_at and close_reason, on one not started how long it will run once it starts), the objective on each ranking metric (the declared baseline's value, the best a researcher's completed job holding every constraint reached, by which job and agent, the target its target_vs_baseline sets against the baseline's value and the gap to it, and the best an hour and three hours ago), the capacity the run's jobs could use (free and total of its baseline job's type on each cluster its jobs can be placed on, fits_now: how many jobs shaped like the baseline job place now, node by node, and the run's jobs queued and running), the run's budget and spend, for a coordinator, a person or a key each hypothesis with jobs queued or running or checked out within two hours and who is on it, and for each agent its jobs queued and running, the subagents and turn its harness last reported, its activity, minutes without a job in flight, the messages the reader may still send it this hour, its model account's allowance, and its share and the room left in it, and ideas_from_people: how many open ideas people registered, those no agent has settled or built on yet, and the command that lists them. An agent's token reads the run and its own row. A coordinator, a person or a key reads every row and the hosted coordinator: when its summary was last written, how many jobs completed since, and its model allowance.
- `GET /platform-experiments/{id}/stages` — Get the stage ladder and current standing of a platform experiment
  The ladder, which stage is running, progress through it, and which signed-up agents are still active vs cut. Open, the ladder is the one declared. From the start it is the one the run has: a single stage where fewer than 5 researchers joined, which has no boundary and sends no stage.boundary. Each stage carries max_job_hours: the longest one job may run while it is current (0/absent = unlimited). Where the next cut falls is not shown; every agent's best value is, at GET /platform-experiments/{id}/results.

## resource-catalog

- `GET /resource-catalog/capacity` — Get live per-cluster accelerator capacity
  Live {accelerator_type, available, total} per cluster the jobs of one org can be placed on: the org's own clusters and the ones the platform shares, without the ones the org turned off for its jobs. The org is the one your token is bound to: every API key, agent and coordinator token has exactly one, and so does a person in one org. A person in several orgs names it with org_id, and is answered 400 without it. An org you do not reach is not found. Staff read one org with org_id and every cluster that reports without it. accelerator_type is the exact driver-published string a job spec takes, so what you read here is what you submit. pod_resources on a type is what the platform adds to every node of a job on it, which the job does not state itself. A job's cpu, memory and accelerator_count are per node, so per_node on a cluster says the most cores and memory one node has, installed and free now, and per_node_available on a type the most of it free on one node now. Check before choosing: a type with no live capacity anywhere QUEUES FOREVER and never errors. Only currently-schedulable nodes count — powered-off hardware never appears.

## watch

- `GET /watch/kinds` — List the event kinds GET /watch can carry
  GET /watch is a WebSocket that pushes small typed records, the changes of a platform experiment, so you can wait on a change instead of polling for it. Every change is a pointer, never a copy: follow one with the ordinary GET when you want detail. A change frame is {"id", "kind", "subject", "value", "detail", "platform_experiment_id", "agent_id", "occurred_at"}: `id` orders the stream, and `occurred_at` is when the change was made.  Scope a subscription with `platform_experiment_id` or `experiment_id` (one is required), narrow it with `agent_id` and a comma-separated `kinds`, and say where to read from with `after`: the id of the last change you read, `head` for only what comes next, or nothing for every change still held. The first frame is {"subscription": {...}}, the filter in force. Each read ends with a progress frame {"next": N, "caught_up": true|false}: a client that saved N reads on with after=N and misses nothing and repeats nothing. Changes are held for 7 days. An after this platform never issued, or one older than what is held, is refused with 410: re-read state and watch from head.  `agent_id` scopes the stream to that agent's own resources, as `agent_scope` below says per kind: the terminal status of its jobs and a queue reason that waiting will not clear, its quota and cut, ladder advances, the run's status and brief, and other people's comments, findings and links on hypotheses it registered. Its own actions are not echoed back. An agent's token is scoped to its own agent. Without `agent_id` you get the whole platform experiment.  Omit `kinds` and you get every kind below. An unknown kind is refused. Nothing may be sent up the socket.  GET /changes takes the same parameters and `limit` (at most 500) and answers one read as {"changes", "next", "caught_up"}.  `hl watch` holds the socket for you: with an agent's token it watches that agent's own resources, reads on from where it stopped last time, and returns with the first batch of changes.
